events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The trip was on the metered RydeTAXI service, so extra kilometres do enter the fare: the meter billed distance $27.13 for 19.2 km, i.e. $27.13 ÷ 19.2 = $1.4130/km, and the trace sets the refund formula as Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4101/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. The rider's complaint is exactly that — a longer way round that cost more than the estimate [F1][F2].

That leaves one question: whether the single off-route segment is exempt. It is not exempt under RD-4: the only traffic records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is band 4 and not band 1 or 2, and no incident was recorded near the route, so there is no qualifying "reasonable cause" corroboration for the replaced stretch [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. The rider also did not request a stop, so RD-3(a) cannot apply to F3 [F7][F8][RD-3].

RD-5 decides it. Before the segment started at 12:27, the driver asked at 12:24 whether he could "go round via Sims Avenue" and named the reason, and the rider replied at 12:24 "Sure, go ahead" [F7][F8][F3]. That is a rider message, sent before the segment, agreeing to a road the driver named; the exchange ties itself by timing to the next off-route segment, which is therefore that Sims Avenue route, and the record shows no different destination — no stop far from that road and no second detour after rejoining [F3][F9][RD-5]. Extra kilometres and distance from the optimal route (5.86 km driven against 2.69 km optimal, +3.17 km) are not evidence of a different excursion; a named alternative road is off the optimal route by definition [F3][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so nothing is left undetermined [F9][RD-5]. The driver's statement merely repeats what the chat already shows and is therefore not needed as the source of consent [F10][RD-5].

The segment F3 is exempt in full, so the sum of non-exempt extra kilometres is 0.00 km and the refund computes as 0.00 km × $1.4101/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. There is no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so no account flag arises [F16][RD-6]. The safety screen found nothing: the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, only a traffic-and-route discussion [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].
